body: The only relevant change is removal of this line, which is redundant, but should not have any significant effect (window position reset later, but I guess can cause some flicker).
I agree, the other changes are more linting than fixes.
I think this will always return the primary screen size, can anyone test picking from a secondary screen that has a different size?

@xsellier Can you please apply this fix in the same PR?

Note:
- we already have `Vector2 offset = ds->mouse_get_position();`, don't know if this one returns the correct screen position, maybe we can reuse `offset` or we get the same screen's position to make it consistent.

<s>Maybe it's better to be done in another PR since it will need testing on all platforms.</s>

> we already have Vector2 offset = ds->mouse_get_position();, don't know if this one returns the correct screen position

It is returning mouse position in desktop coordinates (same for `screen_get_position`), so this is correct.

Tested it on my dual monitor, on Linux, and it worked like a charm. I don't have any recording tho, and haven't tested it on Windows or Mac either ... but I think those changes make sense. So give me a minute and I'm gonna try it again.

> and haven't tested it on Windows or Mac either

This branch is used only on X11.
Let's then wait until someone opens an issue and we track it. Thanks for the fix.
The only difference this change makes is on which side of the cursor preview is shown, it should be usable with or without this change (maybe except screen edges).
Works great, even if I move the Godot windows around between my screens.
There's a bunch more hardcoded values like this in ColorPicker, like `Vector2i(55, 72)` in the `else` branches where `28, 28` is used. It seems a bit weird to special case this one.
I also suggest removing it, unless it will be used to correctly change the popup offset.
Indeed, it probably better to remove it, it's not related to the fix, and if we want to use constants instead of hardcoded sizes/offsets the rest of the values should be changed as well.

I want to improve the code quality of the code I change/write. I don't change something that works without a valid reason.

from my POV, having magic numbers is a bad practice, and should be avoided. Even if the rest of the code keeps using magic numbers, I'd rather start using constant than keep using Magic Numbers.

I'm ok with this PR not merged if you disagree.
